claims.text: The FTC complaint reproduces “Awesome! Cha-ching!” and attributes it to Capitol’s vice president of operations, who became a USAP executive, in the context of expected revenue from repricing Capitol.
The complaint states Welsh Carson created USAP in 2012.

The complaint identifies USAP’s acquisition of Capitol in February 2018 and alleges higher reimbursement rates for the same providers after acquisition; numerical rates and percentage changes are redacted.
The district court granted Welsh Carson’s dismissal motion and denied USAP’s dismissal motion on May 13, 2024. This was not a final merits finding against USAP.
claims.locator: Appended district-court order, Conclusion VI, printed page 23 (PDF page 62)

claims.text: In May 2025 the FTC finalized a separate consent order requiring Welsh Carson to limit its involvement with USAP and notify specified future investments/acquisitions.
The April 23, 2026 joint motion records that USAP denied the allegations.

The FTC announced an agreement in principle with USAP on April 23, 2026; terms were confidential in that announcement. The joint motion states a binding term sheet existed and seeks time for implementation.
claims.locator: Joint motion paragraphs 3–5; announcement opening and third paragraphs

caption:
Texas anesthesia: a quote in the FTC’s 2023 complaint.

“Awesome! Cha-ching!” — attributed in paragraph 164 to Capitol’s vice president of operations, who became a USAP executive, discussing projected repricing revenue. This is a quotation reproduced in a pleading, not an independently verified recording.

The FTC alleged higher reimbursement rates after USAP acquired Capitol in 2018. Public rate figures are redacted; none are estimated here. The complaint states Welsh Carson created USAP in 2012.

Welsh Carson was dismissed from the federal case in 2024. In May 2025, a separate FTC consent order limited its USAP involvement. USAP denied the allegations. On April 23, 2026, the FTC announced a preliminary agreement with USAP.

Coverage ends April 23, 2026. Final implementation and later docket events have not been independently verified. Allegations are not findings.

limitations: The allegations and the reproduced quotation are statements in the FTC pleading, not adjudicated factual findings or an independently authenticated original email.
USAP’s denial, Welsh Carson’s federal dismissal and the separate 2025 FTC consent order must remain in the story.
The April 2026 USAP agreement was preliminary and conditional. Do not describe the settlement as fully implemented.
The document linked by the FTC index as an order granting a stay is an unsigned proposed order in the reviewed PDF. This draft does not claim a judge signed or granted that proposed order.
The agency index was checked October 25, 2026 but last updated April 23. Later docket events have not been independently verified; this is explicitly a historical case file.
No claims of patient deaths, layoffs, specific price percentages or redacted dollar figures are made.
This does not establish that all private-equity ownership produces the same outcomes. The case draft and final assets still require user approval before publication.
